name: Sviten Special
description: Sviten Special (also called Drawmaha) is a Swedish split-pot poker game that combines 5-Card Draw and Pot-Limit Omaha. Each player is dealt 5 cards. There is a Flop, Turn, and River. After the Flop betting, players can discard and draw new cards to their hand (Draw Poker rules). The twist: If you draw ONE card, it is dealt face-up (or you can reject it and take a face-down one). The pot is split between the best 5-card hand (private) and the best Omaha hand (2 private + 3 board).

overview.description: Sviten Special (also called Drawmaha) is a Swedish split-pot poker game that combines 5-Card Draw and Pot-Limit Omaha. Each player is dealt 5 cards. There is a Flop, Turn, and River. After the Flop betting, players can discard and draw new cards to their hand (Draw Poker rules). The twist: If you draw ONE card, it is dealt face-up (or you can reject it and take a face-down one). The pot is split between the best 5-card hand (private) and the best Omaha hand (2 private + 3 board).

history.origins: As reported by Jonas Uebel, Sviten Special became very popular in the Nordic countries and is widely believed to have originated in 2004 at Anders Bengtsson's legendary Sviten poker club in Stockholm. An identical game was played in French Canada in the 1980s as Celestial Poker (Céleste); a similar game is played in the USA as Drawmaha, suggesting the idea arose independently in several places.
history.evolution: The 'One Card Open' rule is the signature Sviten mechanic.

setup.players: Five to seven players; optimum is 5 or 6. Up to 9 can play but the deck may need recycling from the muck for replacements.
setup.deck: Standard international 52-card deck (four suits, Ace through King).
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards each. Small Blind/Big Blind.

rules.objective: Win chips by having the best five-card hand (from your five private cards) and the best Omaha hand (two of your cards plus three board cards) at showdown; the pot is split between these two halves.
rules.gameplay: Blinds are posted. Each player receives five cards and a pre-flop betting round follows. Dealer burns one and deals three community cards (flop); second betting round. Each player may then discard zero to five cards and receive that many replacements from the deck. Dealer burns one and deals the turn card; third betting round. Dealer burns one and deals the river; fourth betting round. At showdown the pot is split between the best five-card hand (private cards only) and the best Omaha hand (exactly two hole cards plus exactly three board cards).
keyRules: Pot limit betting. Blinds and order as in Texas Hold'em and Omaha.
After the flop betting round, each player may discard 0-5 cards and receive an equal number of replacements.
Pot splits between best five-card hand (all five in hand) and best Omaha hand (two from hand, three from board).
Standard poker hand rankings for both halves. One player can scoop the entire pot by winning both halves.

strategy.basic: Start with hands that play well both ways (e.g., A-K-Q-J-10 double suited). Don't draw blindly for a flush if it ruins your Omaha hand. The 'One Open' card gives info to everyoneâ€”if you draw an Ace face-up, everyone knows you have it.
strategy.intermediate: Scooping: You need to win both halves. If you have the Nut Flush in Omaha, and a Pair in hand, you might win half. But Quads in hand and nothing in Omaha is also half. Aim for both.
strategy.advanced: Blockers: Since you see discarded/open cards, use that info. If an opponent draws 1 card and gets a King face-up, you know one King is gone.
tips: Don't fold a Pat Hand too easily.

variations.name: One card face-up
variations.description: When exchanging only one card, the replacement may be dealt face up; the player may accept it or reject it and receive a face-down card instead.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes draw visibility; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Communist Pot
variations.description: Everyone antes 5x the big blind; no betting round after the initial deal - the flop is dealt immediately.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes ante and skips pre-flop bet; overrides can be added when implementing.

variations.name: Roll Your Own
variations.description: Each player reveals one of their five cards when the turn is dealt (before third betting round) and a second when the river is dealt (before final betting round).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes card visibility timing; overrides can be added when implementing.

scoring.description: Pot is split between the best five-card hand (using only the player's five private cards) and the best Omaha hand (exactly two hole cards plus exactly three board cards). Same player can scoop both halves.
scoring.winCondition: Win one or both halves of the pot at showdown: best five-card hand and best Omaha hand (two from hand, three from board). Standard poker hand rankings for both.
